Hospitalization outcomes

Source: vignettes/articles/outcomes.Rmd
outcomes.Rmd

Define discharge outcomes

Use nis_outcomes() on numeric NIS Core fields before building a survey design. It adds three columns and leaves the query in DuckDB. The example uses invented discharges.

Negative HCUP missing-value sentinels and non-integer values become NA in the derived outcomes.

outcomes <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2024)) |>
  nis_outcomes()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpxGrvPQ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpxGrvPQ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

design <- nis_design(
  outcomes,
  cohort = TRUE,
  keep = c(in_hospital_death, los_days, discharge_disposition, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS),
  dollars = 2024
)
#> Cohort: 96 discharges; weighted N 114.4; 12 hospitals across 1 years.
  • In-hospital mortality. in_hospital_death is a logical indicator from DIED. A discharge alive has value FALSE. Missing or invalid DIED stays missing even when a disposition is recorded. The event is death during the sampled hospitalization. HCUP DIED notes
  • Length of stay. los_days uses HCUP’s edited LOS in whole days, including zero for admission and discharge on the same date. Deaths and transfers can have recorded LOS for the sampled stay. HCUP LOS notes
  • Discharge disposition. discharge_disposition holds the numeric DISPUNIFORM code. After collection, nis_label() or nis_design() applies the factor labels. Code 2 denotes transfer to a short-term hospital. Code 5 covers several types of other facilities, including skilled nursing and intermediate care. Code 6 includes home health, home IV, and home hospice. Codes 21 (court/law enforcement) and 99 (alive with destination unknown) are valid categories. An invalid or missing code yields a missing disposition. HCUP DISPUNIFORM notes

These are Core fields on both sides of the 2015 ICD transition. Review the source year’s coding before pooling releases. Historical DISP and detailed billing disposition fields use different codes.

Choose an estimator

For mortality, the survey-weighted mean of the indicator is the proportion of discharges with known status that ended in death. For disposition, use survey-weighted category proportions and state whether the denominator includes in-hospital deaths and the known-alive, unknown-destination group. For skewed LOS, survey quantiles give the median and the 25th and 75th percentiles while retaining same-day stays.

dplyr::summarise(design, mortality = srvyr::survey_mean(in_hospital_death, na.rm = TRUE))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   mortality mortality_se
#>       <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1    0.0201       0.0117
survey::svymean(~discharge_disposition, design, na.rm = TRUE)
#>                                                                               mean
#> discharge_dispositionRoutine discharge to home/self-care                     0.125
#> discharge_dispositionTransfer to another short-term hospital                 0.125
#> discharge_dispositionTransfer to SNF, intermediate care, or another facility 0.125
#> discharge_dispositionHome health care                                        0.125
#> discharge_dispositionLeft against medical advice                             0.125
#> discharge_dispositionDied in hospital                                        0.125
#> discharge_dispositionDischarged/transferred to court/law enforcement         0.125
#> discharge_dispositionAlive, destination unknown                              0.125
#>                                                                              SE
#> discharge_dispositionRoutine discharge to home/self-care                      0
#> discharge_dispositionTransfer to another short-term hospital                  0
#> discharge_dispositionTransfer to SNF, intermediate care, or another facility  0
#> discharge_dispositionHome health care                                         0
#> discharge_dispositionLeft against medical advice                              0
#> discharge_dispositionDied in hospital                                         0
#> discharge_dispositionDischarged/transferred to court/law enforcement          0
#> discharge_dispositionAlive, destination unknown                               0
survey::svyquantile(~los_days, design, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
#> $los_days
#>      quantile ci.2.5 ci.97.5       se
#> 0.25        3      3       4 0.221028
#> 0.5         6      6       7 0.221028
#> 0.75        9      9      10 0.221028
#> 
#> attr(,"hasci")
#> [1] TRUE
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "newsvyquantile"

A geometric mean of LOS requires positive values for the log. If the question concerns positive stays, define that survey domain explicitly and exponentiate its weighted mean log LOS and confidence limits. Report the share of same-day stays and the rule used for zeros. Adding a constant to all stays changes the scale of the quantity being estimated. A NIS heart failure study reported geometric means after substituting a small positive value for zeros, an analysis choice to document when reproducing that study. Heart failure utilization study

Report costs and the analysis denominator

nis_design(..., dollars = 2024) uses the same adjustment as nis_cost() to calculate cost_adj from charges and the hospital cost-to-charge ratio. Report the price index and reference dollar year. Use a survey-weighted arithmetic mean for cost per discharge or a survey-weighted median and quartiles for the distribution of costs.

survey::svymean(~cost_adj, design, na.rm = TRUE)
#>            mean     SE
#> cost_adj 4368.3 54.991
nis_cost_provenance(design)$base_year
#> [1] 2024

For resource use across all discharges, include stays ending in death when LOS or cost is observed. A survivor-only analysis answers a different question. For example, a study of craniotomy costs excluded in-hospital deaths and stays with withdrawal of care, while a pulmonary disease study estimated LOS and costs specifically for stays ending in death. State which population each summary describes. Craniotomy cost study · End-of-life pulmonary hospitalization study

Check and report missingness by outcome and comparison group before using na.rm = TRUE. Each summary then uses its own observed-outcome denominator. Missing or invalid charges or CCRs can leave cost unobserved even for stays with known LOS. A complete-cost summary describes the discharges with calculable costs. If missingness differs by year, group, or survival status, assess how that affects comparisons and any inference to all discharges. One NIS study of prolonged stays used weighted medians and quartiles for non-normal outcomes and complete cases for its mortality regression. Prolonged hospitalization study

See Charges, costs, and provenance and Disclosure review before reporting results.
